doc.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015

title: His first paid gig at $36
summary: Paid $36 in seventh grade on a TV show with a pizza parlor Dixieland band, joining the union and buying hi-hats.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Do you remember the first time you got paid to play?
Yeah. That was in about 1971, ’70. I was in seventh grade.
For my first gig I made $4.

$4? Yeah. And this was actually on a TV show with the local pizza parlor Dixieland band. And so it went through the union too. I had to become a union member, so it had taxes taken out of it and everything.
I felt like, hey, I was in seventh grade. What did I know? $36, that went towards me new pair of hi-hats that cost $100.
